description: Dashboard Earnings Header - Robinhood-style lifetime P/L display with line chart and time range selector

userStories.title: Add daily cumulative P/L data method to PlayerAttentionService
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a method to compute daily cumulative P/L data points so the chart and hero number can display earnings over time.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a struct `DailyPLPoint` with fields `date: Date` and `cumulativePL: Decimal` to PlayerAttentionService.swift
Add static method `dailyCumulativePL(bets: [Bet], days: Int) -> [DailyPLPoint]` to PlayerAttentionService
Method filters to graded bets only (gradeResult != nil, excluding .push)
If days > 0, only include bets from last N days. If days == 0, include all bets.
Group bets by calendar day, compute daily bookie P/L per day: player .win → subtract payout (LiabilityService.calculatePayout), player .loss → add stake
Sort days ascending by date, compute running cumulative sum across days
Return array of DailyPLPoint sorted by date ascending
Handle empty state: return empty array if no graded bets
Also add static method `totalBookiePL(bets: [Bet]) -> Decimal` that returns aggregate lifetime P/L across all players (same logic as realizedPL but without player filter)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Bookie P/L convention: player win = bookie loses payout (negative), player loss = bookie gains stake (positive). Same logic as existing `realizedPL` method but aggregated across ALL players instead of filtering by one player. Use `LiabilityService.calculatePayout(stake:odds:)` for payout calculation. DateFormatter with 'yyyy-MM-dd' for day grouping (same pattern as existing `volatility` method).

userStories.title: Add earnings hero number to dashboard
userStories.description: As a bookie, I want to see my total lifetime earnings as a large, prominent number at the top of my dashboard so I instantly know how much I've made.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove `.navigationTitle("Analytics")` from AnalyticsDashboardView — use `.navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.inline)` with no title or a minimal toolbar approach
Add an earnings header section at the very top of the ScrollView VStack, above the FinishSetupCard and summary cards
Display lifetime P/L using `PlayerAttentionService.totalBookiePL(bets:)` as a large number with `Theme.font(size: 34, weight: .bold)`
Color-code: positive → `Theme.accent`, negative → `Theme.danger`, zero → `Theme.textPrimary`
Format as currency with sign prefix (e.g., '+$1,245.00' or '-$320.50')
Add a smaller label below the hero number showing 'Lifetime P/L' in `Theme.caption` + `Theme.textSecondary`
No card background — render directly on `Theme.background` for an integrated look
Padding: horizontal 16pt to match summary cards
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: This story does NOT include the chart or time range selector — just the big number and label. Keep it simple. The earnings section should be the first thing visible in the ScrollView. The FinishSetupCard (onboarding) should appear below the earnings header if needed. Use the existing `formatCurrency` helper pattern (NumberFormatter with .currency style). The SyncStatusIndicator toolbar item should remain.

userStories.title: Add earnings line chart with Swift Charts
userStories.description: As a bookie, I want to see a line chart of my earnings over time so I can understand my profit trend.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `import Charts` to AnalyticsDashboardView.swift
Add a line chart between the hero number and the summary cards
Use `Chart { LineMark(...) }` with data from `PlayerAttentionService.dailyCumulativePL(bets:days:)`
X-axis: date, Y-axis: cumulative P/L decimal value
Line color: `Theme.accent` if lifetime P/L >= 0, `Theme.danger` if negative
Chart height: 160pt, full width with horizontal padding 16pt matching cards
Hide all axis labels and grid lines for clean Robinhood look: `.chartXAxis(.hidden)` and `.chartYAxis(.hidden)`
Handle empty state: if no data points, show a subtle 'No betting history yet' text in `Theme.textMuted` instead of the chart
Default to showing ALL time data (days: 0)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Swift Charts is available iOS 16+ and app targets iOS 17+ so no compatibility issue. LineMark uses `.value("Date", point.date)` for x and `.value("P/L", NSDecimalNumber(decimal: point.cumulativePL).doubleValue)` for y. Apply `.foregroundStyle(lineColor)` to the LineMark. Use `.interpolationMethod(.catmullRom)` for smooth curves like Robinhood. Extract chart into a private sub-view (e.g., `EarningsChart`) to keep the body manageable and avoid type-checker timeouts.

userStories.title: Add time range selector and period change label
userStories.description: As a bookie, I want to switch between time ranges so I can see my earnings over different periods and know how much I made in each window.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `@State private var selectedRange: String = "ALL"` to AnalyticsDashboardView
Add horizontally arranged time range tabs below the chart: 1W, 1M, 3M, 1Y, ALL
Tabs in an HStack with equal spacing — active tab text uses `Theme.accent` with a small underline or bold weight, inactive uses `Theme.textMuted`
Tab font: `Theme.bodyFont(size: 13, weight: .medium)`
Switching tabs updates the chart data by passing the correct days parameter: 1W=7, 1M=30, 3M=90, 1Y=365, ALL=0
Add `.animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3), value: selectedRange)` for smooth chart transitions
Add a period change label below the hero number (replace or supplement the 'Lifetime P/L' label): shows delta for selected range (e.g., '+$245.00 past 7 days') in green/red with up/down arrow (▲/▼)
Period change = current cumulative P/L minus cumulative P/L at start of the selected range. For ALL, show lifetime total.
Hero number always shows lifetime P/L regardless of selected range
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Time range mapping: '1W' → 7 days, '1M' → 30 days, '3M' → 90 days, '1Y' → 365 days, 'ALL' → 0 (all time). Period change calculation: compute totalBookiePL for all bets, then compute P/L for only bets in the selected range — the difference is the period change. Or simpler: just use realizedPL-style aggregation filtered to the selected range. For the label format: '+$245.00 past 7 days' or '+$1,200.00 all time'. Arrow: ▲ for positive, ▼ for negative, none for zero.
